question: Before cataract surgery, IOL power is calculated using the SRK/T formula. Which TWO measurements are ESSENTIAL inputs for this calculation?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The SRK/T formula requires: (1) axial length measured by A-scan ultrasonography or optical biometry (IOLMaster), and (2) average corneal power (K) measured by keratometry. These two values are the mandatory inputs.

answers.text: Intraocular pressure and anterior chamber depth only

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: IOP measurement is important for surgical safety but is NOT an input to the SRK/T IOL power formula. Anterior chamber depth is used in some third-generation formulas but is not the primary pair.
Visual acuity determines surgical indication but is not a biometric input to IOL formulas. B-scan is used when the posterior segment cannot be visualised, not routinely for IOL calculation.

answers.text: Corneal endothelial cell count and pupil diameter

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Endothelial cell count assesses corneal reserve (relevant for surgical risk) but is not an input to the SRK/T formula. Pupil diameter affects surgical technique, not IOL power.

overallFeedback.feedback: SRK/T formula inputs = axial length (A-scan) + corneal power (keratometry). These biometric measurements, not functional tests, drive the calculation.
Correct. SRK/T needs axial length + K (keratometry). All third-generation formulas share these two primary inputs.
